chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from some of our companions, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), that he
used to say to his companions: 'It is upon you to take up the weapon of the Prophets.' So it was said: 'And what is the weapon of the Prophets?' He said: 'Supplication.'

key_terms.الدُّعَاءُ: Du'a: supplication, the direct address to God in petition or worship
key_terms.سِلَاحُ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ: The weapon of the Prophets — a metaphor for du'a as a means of divine aid and protection
key_terms.عَلَيْكُمْ بِـ: Imperative formula meaning 'it is upon you / you must adhere to' — a strong exhortation

ai.seo_question: What is the weapon of the Prophets according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him), the eighth Imam, habitually exhorted his companions to arm themselves with the weapon used by all the Prophets — supplication (du'a). When asked to identify this weapon, the Imam's concise answer was 'al-du'a' (supplication/prayer). This teaching frames du'a not merely as a devotional act but as a powerful spiritual tool inherited from the prophetic tradition, reminding the community that the Prophets themselves relied on supplication in their struggles.
